What does =SUMIF(A1:A5,"Red",B1:B5) do?
options: Adds the values in B1:B5 where the matching cell in A1:A5 is Red
Counts how many cells contain Red
Adds all the cells in A1:B5
Finds the largest value in B1:B5

questions.q: Cell A1 contains 60. What does =IF(A1>=70,"A",IF(A1>=50,"B","C")) display?
Which feature changes the colour of a cell automatically when its value meets a rule?
A cell shows #NAME?. What is the most likely cause?
options: A function name has been spelled wrongly
A cell used by the formula was deleted

questions.q: Cell C2 contains =B2*$F$1 and is copied down to C3. What does C3 contain?
Data validation can stop users from entering invalid data into a cell.
A what-if model lets you change input values to see the effect on the results.
An absolute reference such as $F$1 changes when it is copied down.
questions.explain: Absolute references stay fixed when copied.

questions.q: VLOOKUP searches the first column of a table for a value and returns data from another column in the same row.
The ____ function adds only the cells that meet a condition.
Changing input values to see how the results change is called ____ analysis.
Rules that limit what can be typed into a cell are called data ____.
The formula =____(A1:A10,">50") counts the cells that are greater than 50.
Explain, with an example, how a nested IF can give three different results.
questions.answer: A second IF is placed inside the first IF (1); example: =IF(A1>=70,"A",IF(A1>=50,"B","C")) (1); gives A, B or C depending on the value (1).

questions.q: Give two data validation rules suitable for a column of test marks out of 100.
questions.answer: Any two from: whole number only; between 0 and 100 (range check); must not be left blank; an error message if the entry is invalid.

questions.q: Describe how a spreadsheet model could be used to plan the budget for a school trip.
questions.answer: Enter costs (transport, tickets, food) and number of students in cells (1); use formulas to work out the total and the cost per student (1); change the inputs (what-if) to see the effect on the cost (1).
